value: Probably named after the village of Tramin (Termeno), around which some of the best wines grow, on warm, calcareous loam in the south of the region.
source_notes: Consortium: Tramin probably gave the variety its name; prefers calcareous loamy soils in warm airy sites in southern South Tyrol. Wine Folly Alto Adige guide: name may come from Tramin (debated); some of the best wines come from around Tramin (Termeno).

value: Here it is mostly made dry, fresher and more structured than its sweet, heady scent suggests, with noticeable acidity.
source_notes: Consortium: traditionally round and full, today fresher and more structured with noticeable acidity. Wine Folly Alto Adige guide: many taste dry despite sweet floral aroma, with more freshness.

value: Made both as a deep red, often aged in oak and labelled Riserva in its sturdiest form, and as a rosé called Kretzer.
source_notes: Consortium: red aged in small oak barrels; rosé version called Lagrein Kretzer. Südtiroler Weinstrasse: Kretzer/rosé style, rose coloured to light ruby, and a full bodied red. Wine Folly Alto Adige guide: Riserva on the label signals a more robust, age worthy Lagrein; oak ageing.

value: Grown throughout the region, often in high vineyards up to about 800 metres.
source_notes: Consortium: widespread in South Tyrol, in high sites up to 800 m. Decanter (premium, read from search excerpt): wines from the poorer soils of higher vineyards show greater intensity, leaner and longer lasting; growers prize its verticality.

value: Here it has lively acidity, and the higher vineyards give leaner, livelier and longer lived wines.
source_notes: Consortium: apple, pear, lemon, hay flower and hazelnut, lively acidity and fruit finesse. Decanter (premium, search excerpt): higher vineyards give leaner, livelier, longer lasting wines; growers prize the verticality of their Pinot Bianco.

value: Here it ranges from full bodied, with ripe apple, pear and quince, to slender and mineral, with lively acidity.
source_notes: Consortium: sometimes fiery and full bodied with ripe apple, pear and quince, sometimes slender and mineral with linden blossom. Wine Folly deep dive: bright, mineral and refreshing with lively acidity.

value: Here it leans to darker woodland berry fruit alongside the red, with a concentrated scent.
source_notes: Consortium: intense scent of red and dark berries, with clove, violet and woodland notes. Südtiroler Weinstrasse: concentrated aroma and flavour reminiscent of woodland berry fruits, long finish.

value: Here it is juicy and low in tannin, often served cool, with a typical almond note on the finish.
source_notes: Consortium: light red with moderate tannin, served chilled as an aperitif. Südtiroler Weinstrasse: low tannin, mild and fruity, often with an almondy aftertaste. Wine Folly deep dive: light, juicy, low in tannin. Kellerei Kaltern (producer, from search excerpt): bitter almond.

value: Grown mostly at middle to high altitude, up to about 600 metres, on calcareous gravel.
source_notes: Consortium: mid to high sites up to 600 m, calcareous gravel soils. Kellerei Kurtatsch (producer, from search excerpt): airy limestone sites at about 450 to 600 m.

value: Here elderflower is a typical note alongside the gooseberry and passion fruit.
source_notes: Consortium: gooseberry, passion fruit, elderflower and blackcurrant. Cantina Tramin (producer, from search excerpt): elderflower and nettle.

value: Here it tends to riper, almost tropical fruit such as pineapple alongside apple and pear, kept fresh by fine acidity.
source_notes: Consortium: pineapple, banana, apple, pear, citrus, vanilla and butter, fine acidity. Cantina Tramin (producer, from search excerpt): fresh and lively, pineapple, pear, citrus, hint of butter.

value: One of the four grapes allowed in Trentodoc, in any proportion, for both the white and the rosé.
source_notes: Italian Wine Central: any proportions of Chardonnay, Pinot Bianco, Pinot Meunier and/or Pinot Nero, for Spumante and Rosato Spumante. Trentodoc consortium: base wine from Chardonnay, Pinot nero, Pinot bianco or Meunier.

value: One of the four grapes allowed in Trentodoc, in any proportion, for both the white and the rosé.
source_notes: As for Chardonnay: four permitted varieties in any proportion, white and rosé.

value: One of the four grapes allowed in Trentodoc, in any proportion, for both the white and the rosé.
source_notes: As for Chardonnay: four permitted varieties in any proportion, white and rosé.

value: One of the four grapes allowed in Trentodoc, in any proportion, for both the white and the rosé.
source_notes: As for Chardonnay: four permitted varieties in any proportion, white and rosé (consortium calls it Meunier, Italian Wine Central Pinot Meunier).

value: Here it goes into sparkling wine, where it adds structure and staying power, above all to the vintage wines and riservas.
source_notes: Consortium: brings structure and longevity to single vintage wines and DOCG riservas; grown on higher, less fertile sites. MICHELIN Guide: used for single vintage wines and rosé cuvées, bringing structure and longevity.

value: Here it gives the sparkling base wines fragrant fruit and flower aromas with good structure and freshness.
source_notes: Consortium: intense, fragrant, complex aroma of fruit and flowers, good structure and pleasant freshness. MICHELIN Guide: valued for aromatic complexity and elegant freshness, mainly for DOCG base wines.

value: A minor partner only: together with Trebbiano di Soave it may make up at most 30 percent of Soave.
source_notes: Italian Wine Central: minimum 70% Garganega; maximum 30% Trebbiano di Soave and/or Chardonnay. SAQ: Garganega at least 70%, remainder may include Trebbiano di Soave and Chardonnay.

value: Here the volcanic basalt hills give firmer, more mineral wines, while limestone sites give more floral ones.
source_notes: SAQ: basaltic terroir gives more minerality and acidity, limestone gives white flowers, apricot and citrus. Consorzio Tutela Vini Soave (sponsored Decanter content): volcanic hills give citrus and almond, calcareous areas more florality and tropical fruit.

value: Grown in the region since the nineteenth century. At least 85 percent of Friuli Cabernet Franc, and it may also go into the Friuli Cabernet blend with Cabernet Sauvignon and Carmenère.
source_notes: Consorzio Friuli Colli Orientali: arrived in Friuli early 1800s, second most widespread black grape in the region; Turismo FVG: in the region from the early 1800s, second most widespread black grape (wording close to the consortium's); Consorzio DOC Friuli: arrived about 1870 from Bordeaux; Friuli DOC production rules art. 2: varietal wines at least 85 percent, Cabernet may combine Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon and Carmenère; Italian Wine Central: same 85 percent and Cabernet blend rule

value: At least 85 percent of Friuli Chardonnay, and one of the four grapes of the Friuli Spumante, with Pinot Bianco, Pinot Grigio and Pinot Nero.
source_notes: Friuli DOC production rules art. 2: varietal minimum 85 percent; Spumante from Chardonnay, Pinot bianco, Pinot grigio, Pinot nero vinified white; Italian Wine Central: same; Consorzio DOC Friuli: Chardonnay can be a still wine or the base for high quality spumante

value: At least 85 percent of Friuli Friulano, which is always a dry wine.
source_notes: Friuli DOC production rules: varietal minimum 85 percent, Friulano sapore asciutto (dry); Italian Wine Central: minimum 85 percent Friulano; Consorzio DOC Friuli: unlike the sweet Hungarian Tokaji, il friulano è secco

value: The most planted red grape of Friuli Venezia Giulia, brought from Bordeaux in the nineteenth century. At least 85 percent of Friuli Merlot.
source_notes: Consorzio DOC Friuli: the most produced red in the region, a French grape brought to Friuli at the end of the 1800s; Consorzio Friuli Colli Orientali: the most widespread black variety in the region; Turismo FVG: born in Bordeaux, king of regional reds since 1880, most widespread black grape; Friuli DOC production rules and Italian Wine Central: varietal minimum 85 percent

value: At least 85 percent of Friuli Pinot Grigio, which may be copper tinted, as ramato, as well as straw yellow.
source_notes: Friuli DOC production rules: varietal minimum 85 percent; Pinot grigio colour straw yellow or ramato, art. 9 allows a copper reflection for Pinot grigio only; Italian Wine Central: Pinot Grigio Ramato at minimum 85 percent; Consorzio DOC Friuli: describes la versione ramata

value: At least 85 percent of Friuli Sauvignon, and the hills of the Colli Orientali and Collio are counted among its best areas.
source_notes: Friuli DOC production rules and Italian Wine Central: varietal minimum 85 percent; Turismo FVG: performs best in the Colli Orientali, Collio and Grave on hillside soils; GuildSomm: suited to the Dolegna subzone of Collio, focus of single vineyard work in the Colli Orientali; Consorzio Friuli Colli Orientali: very favourable soil and climate in the hilly area

value: Sauvignon
source_notes: Friuli DOC production rules: type named Sauvignon o Sauvignon Blanc; Consorzio DOC Friuli: lists the wine as Sauvignon

value: In Friuli it is deeply coloured, full and tannic, with a herbaceous scent that softens as the wine ages.
source_notes: Consorzio Friuli Colli Orientali: full bodied, tannic and herby, loses the herby notes with ageing; Consorzio DOC Friuli: intense deep colour, subtly herbaceous scent, full robust tannic with long maceration; Turismo FVG: herbaceous aromas, full and tannic, improves with age

value: In Friuli it is a structured, velvety dry white with moderate acidity, fuller and softer than the region's Sauvignon.
source_notes: GuildSomm: fuller and lower in acid than Sauvignon, ripe fleshy fruit; Consorzio Friuli Colli Orientali: dry, intense, velvety, generally moderate acidity; Turismo FVG: an elegant, structured white

value: In Friuli it makes dry, structured and savoury reds, which gain in refinement with age.
source_notes: Consorzio DOC Friuli: dry, full bodied, harmonious, sapido (savoury); Turismo FVG: structure and sapidità that improve with age; Consorzio Friuli Colli Orientali: structured and tangy, becomes refined with ageing

value: On the Friuli hills it gives very fresh, tart whites with a mineral, almost salty edge and delicate white flower scents.
source_notes: Turismo FVG: best on the hills, stands out for freshness, minerality, refined floral bouquet; GuildSomm: can be cruelly tart with mild flavours of white flowers and salt; Consorzio DOC Friuli: dry, rich in acidity, very pleasant freshness

value: In Friuli it makes full bodied, well structured whites with good acidity.
source_notes: Turismo FVG: full bodied and well structured, yellow flowers, sage and bell pepper; Consorzio Friuli Colli Orientali: structured, full bodied and characteristic with good acidity

value: At least 85 percent of Friuli Colli Orientali Chardonnay, and with Pinot Bianco it makes up 20 to 30 percent of the Rosazzo DOCG white.
source_notes: Friuli Colli Orientali production rules and Italian Wine Central: varietal minimum 85 percent; Rosazzo DOCG production rules art. 2: Pinot bianco and/or Chardonnay 20 to 30 percent, Friulano at least 50; GuildSomm: Chardonnay a supporting variety in Rosazzo DOCG

value: At least 85 percent of Friuli Colli Orientali Merlot, which may be labelled Riserva after two years of ageing.
source_notes: Friuli Colli Orientali production rules art. 2 and 7: varietal minimum 85 percent; Riserva after at least two years from 1 November of the harvest year; Italian Wine Central: Merlot minimum 85 percent, Riserva minimum 2 years

value: At least 85 percent of Friuli Colli Orientali Sauvignon, and 20 to 30 percent of the Rosazzo DOCG white.
source_notes: Friuli Colli Orientali production rules and Italian Wine Central: varietal minimum 85 percent; Rosazzo DOCG production rules: Sauvignon 20 to 30 percent; GuildSomm: Sauvignon one of the permitted white varieties in Rosazzo DOCG

value: Sauvignon
source_notes: Friuli Colli Orientali production rules: type named Sauvignon o Sauvignon blanc; Consorzio Friuli Colli Orientali: lists the wine as Sauvignon

value: In the Colli Orientali it is dry, full and savoury, with a tangy freshness, and it grows more refined with age.
source_notes: Friuli Colli Orientali production rules art. 6: Merlot sapore asciutto, pieno, sapido; Consorzio Friuli Colli Orientali: structured and tangy, refined and more complex with ageing

value: Here it is delicately rather than richly sweet, warm and smooth, with enough acidity that the finish reads almost dry.
source_notes: GuildSomm: delicately sweet, with enough acidity to finish dry; Consorzio Friuli Colli Orientali: sweet, harmonious, pleasantly greasy and balanced; Picolit DOCG production rules: sapore amabile o dolce, caldo, armonico, delicato, art. 9 calls it dolce non dolce

value: In the Colli Orientali it is made dry and full bodied, with a harmonious, lingering palate.
source_notes: Friuli Colli Orientali production rules art. 6: Pinot grigio sapore asciutto, pieno, armonico; Consorzio Friuli Colli Orientali: a dry, lingering, full bodied taste with a pleasantly tart aftertaste

value: Here it is velvety and soft in tannin, with lively acidity and small red fruit, and the Prepotto wines carry a note of green pepper.
source_notes: Friuli Colli Orientali production rules: Schioppettino vellutato, pieno, secco, small fruits; Schioppettino di Prepotto annex: vellutato, di corpo, secco, con sentore di pepe verde, spices and small fruits; GuildSomm: pomegranate and raspberry, soft tannins, lively acidity; Consorzio Friuli Colli Orientali: intense and spicy

value: From an inland valley with a continental climate and cool nights, Matelica gives a fresher Verdicchio with firmer acidity than the Jesi wines nearer the coast.
source_notes: Decanter: Matelica 'much prized for its greater aromatic intensity and its firmer acidity'; less maritime influence, cooler nights preserve acidity. Gilbert & Gaillard: Matelica continental climate, wines 'fresher and more mineral, with greater acidity' than Castelli di Jesi.

value: Closer to the sea and on heavier clay, Jesi Verdicchio tends to be rounder and more powerful, with sunnier fruit than the leaner wines of Matelica.
source_notes: Decanter: Jesi soils heavy clay; 'the power and intensity of wines from Jesi' versus 'finesse and longevity' of Matelica. Gilbert & Gaillard: Jesi Mediterranean climate near the sea, wines 'sunnier and more Mediterranean, with fruity notes and a well rounded structure'; both note exceptions within Jesi.

value: Etna Carricante ages remarkably for a white without oak, moving from a nervy, salty youth to a honeyed, smoky maturity often likened to aged Riesling.
source_notes: Decanter: Carricante has a 'Riesling like ability to age, mutating from nervy saltiness to honeyed, smoky maturity, without any assistance from oak'. Wine Scholar Guild: young Carricante has a smoky, saline finish; with age it gains honey, preserved lemon, almond and beeswax and at its finest rivals great Riesling.

value: On thin soils of steep alpine terraces, Nebbiolo here is more perfumed and lighter bodied than in Barolo and Barbaresco, and wears its tannins more lightly.
source_notes: Decanter: Nino Negri's Casimiro Maule, 'our soils are very thin and our wines are more perfumed, elegant, and lighter bodied' than Piedmont; 'the wines also wear their tannins lightly'. Wine Enthusiast (page blocks automated fetch, read from search excerpt): wines 'naturally lighter on their feet' with lower alcohol than Barolo and Barbaresco, more delicate tannins than the Langhe.

value: On the weathered granite of Sardinia's northeast, Vermentino di Gallura is more intense and less overtly fruity than the island's other Vermentino, with mineral and floral notes.
source_notes: Decanter: Gallura has wide day night swings and weathered granite soil; 'the resulting wines are intense and minerally rather than overtly fruity'. Sardegna Turismo (regional tourism board): Gallura's stricter rules make 'the aroma more flavourful and flowery', while Vermentino di Sardegna 'provides fruitier notes'.

value: Grown across the island on limestone, marl and granite, Vermentino di Sardegna is usually fruitier and more direct than the granite grown wines of Gallura.
source_notes: Sardegna Turismo: Vermentino di Sardegna 'provides fruitier notes' than Gallura; grows on granite and on chalky, clay rich soils. Decanter: Gallura is minerally 'rather than overtly fruity', the contrast implied. Wine With Seth (lower tier): the island wide DOC spans limestone and marl in the south to granite in the north and gives fresher, lighter styles than Gallura.

value: Cannonau keeps a warm, spicy, earthy Mediterranean character, but many Sardinian producers now make it finer and fresher than the robust style of the past, with silky tannins.
source_notes: Decanter: Cannonau 'captures the island's generous warmth, producing plush, spicy and earthy reds'; producer Antonella Corda: more freshness than many Grenache because harvested earlier. Gambero Rosso (2025): long 'robusto, caldo e generoso', now made finer with silky tannins and preserved freshness and acidity, keeping its spicy Mediterranean soul.

value: Picked late, often in November, in hills where nights are cool, Taurasi Aglianico gains a savoury ripeness while keeping a fresh, almost saline acidity.
source_notes: Decanter buyer's guide: harvest usually late October, sometimes November, 'one of the last harvests in all of Italy'; grapes reach 'savoury maturity'; supple tannins 'underpinned by refreshing, saline acidity'; day night swings key to freshness. Wine Scholar Guild Campania vintage chart: harvest culminating in Taurasi in November in some years; wide day night gap giving very good acidity (vintage specific entries).

value: Greco di Tufo has an unusual grip for a white, with a firm acid spine, a pleasant bitterness and a light tannic texture, and it needs time in bottle to show its complexity.
source_notes: World of Fine Wine (Sarah Marsh MW): 'a firm acid spine, austerity, appetizing bitterness, and tannic grip', 'more like a red than a white'; Greco needs age; Fiano the more delicate and aromatic. Vinorandum (lower tier, via search excerpt): firm acidity and a textured, slightly tannic structure, more phenolic grip than Fiano.
